title: All Good Things: tasting three examples from this new supermarket-targeted brand
summary: All Good Things This is a new brand focusing on Australia and New Zealand, with appealing, direct packaging. They are
content:
All Good Things

This is a new brand focusing on Australia and New Zealand, with appealing, direct packaging. They are designed for supermarket shelves and there’s some promotional wiggle in the pricing it seems (the list price is somewhat inflated to allow regular discounting to drive sales: they are listed at £9.75-10, but seem to be selling at £8).

All Good Things Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Western Australia
12% alcohol. Zesty citrussy nose is bright and fruity, although there’s not a lot of Sauvignon Blanc character. The palate is light and fruity, with bright lemon and pear fruit, but it’s a bit dilute. Perfectly OK, if you are looking for a generic, crisp dry white wine. 81/100

All Good Things Sauvignon Blanc 2025 Marlborough, New Zealand
12.5% alcohol. There’s some trade-mark elderflower and citrus zest on the nose with a hint of green. The palate is juicy and lively, with nice depth of fruit and good acidity, as well as a touch of sweetness that rounds things out. This tastes of Marlborough Sauvignon. 87/100

All Good Things Shiraz 2024 Western Australia
13.5% alcohol. Spice, chocolate and red berries on the nose, which is sweet and appealing. The palate has rounded berry fruit with a touch of coffee and vanilla adding a nice framing, and a bit of complexity. Some mint/eucalypt character too, with the sweet fruit coming to the fore on the finish. Cleverly put together, this has broad appeal. 86/100

title: Canadian Sparkling Wine: a rare tasting crossing the country, with 24 different wines
summary: Canadian Sparkling Wine is a category that is progressing nicely. This tasting was a selection of 24, across many different
content:
Canadian Sparkling Wine is a category that is progressing nicely. This tasting was a selection of 24, across many different regions. Because of laws restricting inter-provincial shipping of wine, it’s difficult to get a line-up like this. These aren’t all of the best fizzes that Canada makes, but it’s a nice selection showing some of the diversity, with some real highlights. Niagara is slightly over-represented here because this is where the tasting took place.

NIAGARA

Trius Brut NV Niagara, Canada
50% from 2024, and 75% Chardonnay, 25% Pinot Noir. Bright and fresh with nice citrus drive. This has great balance and is fruit driven. Juicy, fresh and very tasty. 90/100

Trius Showcase Blanc de Blancs NV Niagara, Canada
This is a blend of 2011, 2012 and 2013, raised in neutral French oak, then 10 years on lees before being disgorged in September 2024. Lovely focused citrus nose is very pure, with nice toasty detail, and notes of bread and salt. Lively, linear and focused with real complexity and finesse. 93/100

Kew Vineyards Tradition 2021 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
4 g/l dosage. Fruity and bright with nice detail. Has pear and a touch of peach, showing warmth and balance. 89/100

Kew Vineyards Blanc de Blancs 2021 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Lovely bright lemony fruit with some pear and apple. Fruity with nice density, and a touch of richness. 88/100

Kew Vineyards Blanc de Noirs 2020 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Pinot Noir. Cherries and spice with nice density. Rich with some fruit sweetness and some spiciness. 90/100

Kew Vineyards Rosalie 2019 Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
Skin contact Pinot Noir. Sweet and sour with cherries and spice, as well as a nice citrus drive, and a touch of orange peel. 89/100

Westcott Brilliant 2020 Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
45% Pinot Noir, 45% Chardonnay, 10% Pinot Meunier. Base wine has 10% barrel fermentation, wild ferment for all base wine. Four years on lees then disgorged with 5 g/l dosage. Lovely citrus drive with impact, and a touch of pithiness under the lively lemony fruit. Nice depth and intensity here. 92/100

Westcott Brilliant Blanc de Noirs NV Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
Two-thirds 2020 and one-third perpetual reserve. Barrel fermented in puncheons on the previous year’s lees. Freeze some juice for the liqueur for tirage, no adding yeast at this stage. Creamy and toasty with nice texture and some warmth. Some toast from the barrel ferment and a touch of spice. Broad, satisfying and refined. 93/100

York Brut NV Niagara on the Lake, Canada
This is 2018, the first vintage, although it is labelled NV. Focused, fresh and taut with nice lemony fruit, but also a bit of richness. Powerful with nice density. Stylish. 92/100

York Brut Rosé NV Niagara on the Lake, Canada
2017, first vintage, 100% Pinot Noir, short skin maceration to get colour. Fruity and fine with notes of orange peel, pear and citrus. Has some subtle toast. Textured and quite luxurious. 92/100

York Reserve 2016 Niagara on the Lake, Canada
60% Chardonnay, 40% Pinot Noir, base wine has 2 years in older French oak. Then 6 years on lees. This is complex and layered, toasty and lively. Nice peach, spice, pear and citrus with real complexity and power. 94/100

Malivoire Bisous Brut NV Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
70% Chardonnay, 23% Pinot Noir, 7% Pinot Gris. 2020 base, 3 years on lees, 6 g/l dosage. Fresh, bright and pithy with nice citrus drive. Fruity and expressive. Tart and linear with a juicy finish. 91/100

Malivoire Bisous Blanc de Gamay 2023 Vinemount Ridge, Niagara, Canada
One year on lees after base wine aged in used French oak, 6 g/l dosage. Taut, fresh and linear with some bright pithiness and a touch of cherry on the nose. Juicy, herby palate with nice brightness. Has a slight saltiness. 90/100

Malivoire Bisous Rosé NV Beamsville Bench, Niagara, Canada
2023 base year, 2 years on lees, 8 g/l dosage. Very pale with lovely juiciness and tight cherry fruit with a good citrus drive. Juicy and fruity with a slight saltiness and nice purity. 91/100

Malivoire Bisous Noir 2023 West Niagara, Canada
75% Pinot Noir, 25% Gamay, one week on skins, one year on lees. Red in colour, this is fruity and bright with lively cherry and plum fruit. Nice red fruit character. Juicy and refined, lovely stuff. 92/100

QUEBEC

Domaine Saint Jacques Brut 2023 Quebec, Canada
24 months on lees, a blend of Chardonnay and Vidal. Fruity and bright with nice lemon and pear fruit. Juicy and linear with good acidity and admirable purity of fruit. Refined. 91/100

Domaine Bergeville Le Blanc 2024 Quebec, Canada
Some unusual notes on the nose: I thought it might be corked, but it wasn’t. Herbal, lemony and bright with pear and peach fruit as well as some pithiness. Juicy with some complexity, and quite distinctive. 88/100

NOVA SCOTIA

Benjamin Bridge Methode Classique NV Nova Scotia, Canada
11% alcohol. A blend of grapes including some hybrid in this cuvée. Fresh and linear with nice pithy hints. Tart and lively with a lovely lemony drive, some tightness and a slight herby character. Saline twist on the finish. Very fine. 93/100

Avondale Sky Blanc de Noir 2017 Nova Scotia, Canada
Fresh, fruity and lively with nice herb and toast complexity. Rich and layered with lots of flavour. 90/100

L’Acadie Prestige Brut 2019 Nova Scotia, Canada
Juicy, bright and fresh with nice pithiness. Some grapey richness as well as focused lemony fruit. Bright and linear with nice precision. 90/100

VANCOUVER ISLAND

Blue Grouse Sparkling Cuvée 2020 Cowichan Valley, Vancouver Island, Canada
Fruity, bright and linear with nice lemon and herb notes. Tart and lively with nice precision. 89/100

OKANAGAN/SIMILKAMEEN/FRASER VALLEY

Corcelettes MT 2022 Similkameen, BC, Canada
Juicy, bright and lemony with tartness and good acidity. Nice fruitiness here with a  good acid line. 88/100

Terravista Vineyards En Terre 2022 Okanagan, BC, Canada
Juicy and bright with nice cherry and citrus fruit, with a compact character. Lively, bright and stylish. 91/100

Township 7 Sirius 2017 Fraser Valley, BC, Canada
Focused and quite toasty, showing nice complexity. There’s a saline edge to the focused citrus fruit, as well as some spicy complexity. Stylish 93/100

title: Highlights: Dow’s Vintage Port 2024 Douro, Portugal
summary: Isn’t Port wonderful? And Vintage Port, the pinnacle of the Port world, can even be drunk young. I reckon it’s
content:
Isn’t Port wonderful? And Vintage Port, the pinnacle of the Port world, can even be drunk young. I reckon it’s best drunk young, for all its immediacy, or then let it go through its middle age and then approach it in its mellow maturity. The thing is, this maturity stretches long, and Port has this sort of immortality to it, where it’s incredibly rare to find a Port that’s not got anything left to give.

Dow’s Vintage Port 2024 Douro, Portugal
20% alcohol. From Quinta do Bomfim in the Cima Corgo and Quinta da Senhora da Ribeira in the Douro Superior. 40% Touriga Franca, 35% Touriga Nacional, 15% field blend (old vines) and 10% Alicante Bouschet. 99 g/l rs which is drier on the spectrum. Amazing aromatics. So intense with black cherries, blackcurrant and some smoky spiciness, and a touch of pepper, and even a bit of ginger on the finish. Olive, tar and spice as well as fragrant fruit. Lush and brooding on the palate with lots of sweetness as well as some spicy tannin. Concentrated and intense, and particularly sweet and rich, and sweeter than you might expect from Dow’s, although the sugar isn’t very high. This is quite brilliant. It’s so lush and vibrant, with such floral fruit. There’s some tannin here, but it’s amazingly approachable for a serious vintage Port. I think it will pick up some weight in bottle, and have a long life, but this might be a wonderful Port young, middle-aged and old. 97/100

title: Highlights: Markus Altenburger Chardonnay Vom Kalk 2024 Austria
summary: I bought this from an amazing neighbourhood grocery shop – Lauriston Grocers in Victoria Park. As well as a great
content:
I bought this from an amazing neighbourhood grocery shop – Lauriston Grocers in Victoria Park. As well as a great array of fresh produce, they have a brilliant wine selection, through an association with Newcomer Wines.

Markus Altenburger Chardonnay Vom Kalk 2024 Austria
12.5% alcohol. This Burgenland Chardonnay is brilliant. It’s beautifully aromatic with some chalky lime fruit and a hint of ripe apple. The palate is ripe and rich but also has real energy and a fresh, chalky, minerally edge, as well as pear, peach and ripe apple characters. Beautiful elegance and tension here, showing depth but also elegance. This is such a lovely wine. 94/100

title: Eight wines under £10 that offer amazing value, from The Wine Society
summary: It’s getting very hard to find wines that retail under £10 in the UK and which still have any character,
content:
It’s getting very hard to find wines that retail under £10 in the UK and which still have any character, because of the recent increase in taxation. But The Wine Society seem to have a gift for sniffing out bargains, and I have pulled out a few gems here from yesterday’s excellent press tasting.

Lou Blanc Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh 2022 France
14% alcohol. This is made by Plaimont and it’s a blend of Gros Manseng, Petit Manseng and Petit Courbu, stainless steel fermented and aged. Weighty and delicious, this is layered with honeyed citrus and pear fruit. The fruit has a sweetness to it (although it’s a dry wine), and everything is nicely hemmed in by spicy acidity. 92/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

Emiliana Silbador Gewurztraminer 2025 Rapel, Chile
13% alcohol. Made by organic specialists Emiliana. This is a beautiful Gewurztraminer with rose petal, pear and lychee notes. It’s not too showy, and comes across as fresh and pure with nice depth. Dry. 91/100 (£8.95 The Wine Society)

Domaine Emile Boeckel Alsace Blanc 2025 France
12.5% alcohol. A blend of Sylvaner, Muscat and Pinot Blanc. This is beautifully expressive with some grapey, lychee prettiness and also notes of honey, peach and pear. Delicious stuff with just a hint of sweetness (rs 6.2 g/litre). Impressive for the price. 90/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

Château Beaubois Un Amour de Cinsault 2025 France
11.5% alcohol. From the Costières de Nîmes this is a biodynamic Cinsault of real class. Fresh raspberry and cherry fruit nose with some wild herbs. Very Cinsault in character. The palate is pure and focused with nice balance to the fresh red cherry and plum fruit. 92/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

Feudo Arancio Nero d’Avola 2024 Sicily, Italy
13% alcohol. This carries 6.3 g/l residual sugar, but I didn’t spot it. There’s lovely fruit purity with cherries, raspberries and a lick of spice and pepper. Nice weight: this is just about the pure fruit. 90/100 (£9.25 The Wine Society)

The Society’s Barbera d’Asti Superiore 2023 Piemonte, Italy
13% alcohol. I was really impressed by this own-label Barbera. Lovely weight and balance here with nice density and a wet stone edge to the pure cherry and plum fruit. Good concentration and superb balance. 91/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

AA Badenhorst Fontein Cabernet Sauvignon Syrah 2026 Swartland, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. A lovely fresh, drinkable baby wine (this is 2026!). Fresh, floral, expressive nose is juicy and bright with nice grip, as well as supple, open cherry and strawberry fruit. Delicious with lovely drinkability and a bit of grip on the finish. 91/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

Undurraga Candelabro Carmenere 2025 Maule, Chile
14% alcohol. This is brilliant. Fresh, floral blackcurrant fruit with some cherry and spice. Nice freshness on the palate with some structure, showing lovely vivid, sweet fruit and nice brightness. 92/100 (£9.95 The Wine Society)

title: Visiting Montes, a major Chilean winery who are making the switch to regenerative viticulture
summary: I visited Montes with Rodrigo Barral chief viticulturist and Santiago Izcúe, winemaker. It was an interesting visit: this is a
content:
I visited Montes with Rodrigo Barral chief viticulturist and Santiago Izcúe, winemaker. It was an interesting visit: this is a rather special vineyard, with the main part of the property consisting of an amphitheatre-like arrangement of vines on hillsides at the end of the Apalta Valley in Colchagua. It’s varied and quite beautiful.

Montes has 120 hectares of vines here in Apalta, plus another 450 in Marchigüe, also in Colchagua but closer to the ocean, so a cooler site. They also have the 47 hectare Zapallar vineyard in coastal Acongcagua. The project dates back to the late 1980s, when it was founded by Aurelio Montes and a couple of partners, and has grown significantly since then.

Four years ago, Aurelio Montes asked Rodrigo to look at converting the vineyards to organics. But Rodrigo says that this didn’t sit well with him. The motivation for this was that they were becoming concerned about the resilience of the vineyard. A look at the chart plotting GDDs over the last 24 years showed that there was a slow rise, but from 2015 the seasons have varied a lot, with a big fluctuation of el niño and el niña years. In terms of GDDs the cooler seasons are below 1600, and the warmer ones past 1800, and with these fluctuations there’s quite a variation in rainfall. Climate chaos is the new normal!

Rodrigo had been to a seminar on climate change and regenerative farming, and decided that rather than heading down the organic path, a switch to regenerative would be the best route to take, because it promises to increase the resilience of the vineyard. So this is what they have done.

Vermicasting is an interesting process. Unlike normal warm composting, it’s a cold process that doesn’t generate a lot of heat. It is usually done with a species of worm called Eisenia fetida, also known as the red wriggler, and it’s a surface dwelling epigeic worm well suited to this task.

They produce vermicast using the Biofiltro system that I’ve written about before. This is a 30 x 40 metre plot where they use wood chips and cardboard waste, and water it with minimally treated winery waste water. The worms break down the wood and cardboard, cleaning the waste water in the process, and this is of the quality to be used for irrigation. And a by-product is the black gold: vermicast.

Another thing they do is to make JADAM compost tea. This is a cheap and effective way of culturing microorganisms that you can then add back to the soil.

For composting, they use wool and grape marc, and mix in some vermicast. They control the temperature because they want lots of fungus, and if the temperature gets too high the fungus is lost. 500 m3 ends up as 250 m3 at the end of the process. They use it at a concentration of 4 tonnes/hectare in new blocks and any weaker blocks.

They are still learning about cover cropping and managing them in this site. They use a roller crimper to terminate the cover crop as the vines get going, and a finger weeder for undervine.  ‘The weeds were our enemies,’ says Rodrigo, ‘but now they help us to have the natural balance in the whole vineyard.’

They have been measuring fungi, bacteria and protozoa in the soils from 2023. The new farming regime has had measurable impact. Potassium increased 31% and phosphorus 22%, so they no longer have to add these as inputs. Overall, they have reduced inputs in Apalta by 31%, and in Marchigüe they are down 54%. They no longer use any herbicides in Apalta, and they’ve reduced herbicide use in the much larger Marchigüe vineyard by 49%.

One of the goals of regenerative farming is increasing soil organic material. This also has a side-benefit of reducing atmospheric carbon dioxide. Rodrigo showed me some data. In first 30 cm of soil, if you increase organic matter by 1% this stores 83 tonnes of CO2 per hectare. If we do this in all agricultural soils in the world, he points out, then we’ll be storing 130 gigatons, mitigating 7 years of CO2 rises. When they started the regenerative program, their soil organic material was 1.5% and three years later it is 3%. Adding +0.4% organic material per year offsets all their carbon dioxide emissions.

THE WINES

Outer Limits Albariño 2025 Zapallar, Aconcagua
This is 7 km from the Ocean and has a strong cooling influence, and it works well for Albariño. Natural decantation, 80 NTUs so the juice is very clean, 14 C fermentation temperature in stainless steel. This is pure, vivid and quite primary with crisp, clean citrus fruit and some pear drop esters from the fermentation still. Fresh and crystalline with a touch or apricot. 90/100

Outer Limits Sauvignon Blanc 2024 Zapallar, Aconcagua
12 h cold maceration, natural decanting, long fermentation at low temperature. Bottle young. Chalky and a bit green on the nose. Vivid citrussy fruit with a touch of elderflower. Good concentration with well-integrated green notes and good acidity, and a nice chalky edge. 88/100

Outer Limits Pinot Noir 2023 Zapallar, Acongcagua
One tank is carbonic (100%, pressed and finished fermentation in liquid phase), second tank is destemmed, third is stems added back in layers. This makes three different wines. This is silky and fruity with nice complexity: there’s sweet cherry fruit but also hints of undergrowth and spice. It’s warm and spicy, but also fresh and quite layered. A lovely Pinot Noir. 93/100

Outer Limits CGM 2024 Apalta, Colchagua
Carigan, Grenache and Mourvèdre from Apalta. Use gravity instead of pumps. They use commercial yeasts. Stainless steel for fermentation, 3 pump overs a day (short and gentle), short macerations. Rack into concrete eggs and old barrels, in order to get some softness. This is juicy and energetic with vivid black cherry and blackberry fruit with some firm, grippy tannins and good acidity. Juicy and linear with a touch of pepper on the finish. 93/100

Montes Alpha Cabernet Sauvignon 2015 Colchagua
15% Merlot in the blend. 50% new French oak. This has a powerful nose of mint and blackcurrant with a hint of vinyl and tar. Intriguing. The palate is still youthful with some dusty blackcurrant fruit and good structure, as well as bright acidity. Very minty! Nice balance here with a remarkable personality, and still with potential for further development. 93/100

Purple Angel by Montes Carmenère 2021 Colchagua
92% Carmenère, 8% Petit Verdot. Aged in French oak, 70% new. This is benchmark Carmenère with ripe blackcurrant fruit, some chalkiness, and then black cherries, some mulchy leafy characters, fig and pepper, with some grippy tannin. There’s a lovely density and intensity to this wine, with black fruits to the fore and a hint of blackberry jam. This has a lot of personality, and the oak is just swallowed up by the fruit, with a nice mouthfeel. 94/100

title: Arnaldo Rivera, a top tier of wines from the overperforming Terre del Barolo cooperative
summary: Websites: https://terredelbarolo.com/en/  https://arnaldorivera.com/en/ The Terre del Barolo cooperative was founded in 1958 in Castiglione. First vintage was 1959, and today
content:
Websites: https://terredelbarolo.com/en/  https://arnaldorivera.com/en/

The Terre del Barolo cooperative was founded in 1958 in Castiglione. First vintage was 1959, and today they are an important player in the region. In 2017 they began the Arnaldo Rivera project, named after the founder of the cooperative. I met with Gabriele Oderda, Director of Arnaldo Rivera, on a video call, to chat through this interesting project while tasting five wines.

Gabriele emphasized that understanding Arnoldo Rivera today requires an understanding of how Barolo has developed as a region. These days, it’s famous and the top wines are expensive, but this wasn’t always the case.

After the second world war, Langhe was one of poorest agricultural areas of all northern Italy. This isn’t all that long ago. It was in 1958 that Arnaldo Rivera began the cooperative Terre del Barolo. He was an important figure in the region and for 37 years was mayor of Castiglione Faletto. ‘He was a man of the people, the guy that you want to call for an advice,’ says Gabriele. ‘This was the time when Giacomo Oddero was mayor in La Mora, Battista Rinaldi was mayor in Barolo and Giovanni Gaja was mayor in Barbaresco. It was an all-star game. These are the founding fathers of the modern Barolo. And also Arnaldo Rivera during his lifetime was one of the closest friends of Bartolo Mascarello himself. But he did something different from all these people. He didn’t put his own family name on the label. But he put the community ahead. And he thought of building a winery for the people.’

One of the motivations for forming the cooperative was because of how badly the growers were being treated in the grape market of Alba. ‘It was known locally as the dead people market, because of the depreciation in the price of the grapes,’ says Gabriele. ‘The grape market was ruled by just a few brokers.’

What happened in Barolo opened the path for quality, says Gabriele. In contrast, things didn’t work out so well in the north of Piemonte. At the beginning of the 20th century this northern part of the region was one of the most intensively planted regions in Italy, but a lot of the vineyards have now gone. Workers left from the vineyards to the textile industry and to the cities. This could have happened to the Langhe, too, but it didn’t.

Terre del Barolo is the only grower cooperative in Barolo. When Analdo Rivera founded it, only 22 growers joined the first year. The next year, 250 joined. ‘We are a little bit like the sheep in Italy, we never move,’ says Gabriele. ‘We look around, but we don’t move. If one starts to go, everyone follows. So, as soon as they started to build a winery, in the springtime of 1959, there was a big attraction towards the coop.’

Arnaldo Rivera stipulated some conditions for those who wanted to join. They needed to be located in one of the 11 villages of Barolo, they needed to own their vineyards, and all their grapes had to come to the cooperative. And the grapes needed to come to the cooperative in small boxes, with no pressing at the farm. This allows the strict control of quality.

The cooperative is significant for the region, making 12% of all Barolo. The whole appellation is 2200 hectares, and cooperative members have 240 of these.

Terre del Barolo have a number of tiers of quality, in a sort of pyramid. At the bottom is bulk wine, sold to supermarkets and big players, enabling them to get quality at a good price. Then there’s middle range, which is the core of their production. And the top tier is around 10% of production, and this is Arnoldo Rivera, which is a completely separate philosophy, based on vineyard-designated wines. 35 of the 300 growers Terre del Barolo contribute to this tier. They are paid according to the potential yield of their site, so it is about enabling them to farm well, with a specific vineyard protocol. ‘This Arnaldo Rivera philosophy was born from the bottom,’ says Gabriele. ‘This is not a director’s marketing programme.’

As well as Barolo, they have added some interesting grape varieties to the range, including Freisa, Verduno Pelaverga, Dolcetto and Nascetta (a rare white variety).

I asked Gabriele about where the cooperative sat on the modernist/traditionalist Barolo discussions of the past. ‘Our winery is a farmer cooperatives. And when we think about taking a decision with the 300 heads, this is very time consuming. Sometimes being slow provides luck!’ So they didn’t jump on the modernist small-oak bandwagon. ‘We passed the trend. We didn’t even notice.’ They stuck with the large-format wooden casks. But when they stared started Arnoldo Rivera ten years ago they had to buy some smaller vessels because they were dealing with small plot vinifications. ‘We have Rocche Castiglione, which is a vineyard of 0.34 hectares. We cannot fill a large cask.’ For smaller oak, they are very careful about the barrels, they test the staves and everything is not toasted, but staves are bent by vapour and not fire to limit the impact on the wine.

Arnaldo Rivera Langhe Nascetta del Commune di Novello 2024 Piemonte, Italy
13% alcohol. Nascetta is a rare variety that’s unique to the commune of Novello in Barolo. No oak here, but an extra year in bottle to help subdue some of the more floral terpenic notes. This is textured and quite broad with a subtly spicy edge to the rich pear and white peach fruit. It’s a really classy, full-flavoured wine, but has balance. Subtle notes of wax and toast, and some aniseed and sour cherry on the finish. Bold and quite delicious. 93/100

Arnaldo Rivera Undicicomuni Barolo 2022 Piemonte, Italy
14.5% alcohol. Potentially from all 11 communes in Barolo (they are the only producer to have grapes from all of them, but it wasn’t until 2025 that all made it into the blend), two years in large oak. This is rich, ripe and textured with some warm spiciness and nice structure under the red cherry and cranberry fruit, and there’s also a floral dimension on the nose. There’s some richness here, but it isn’t a heavy wine. The alcohol makes its presence felt, and the fruit sweetness coats the tannins. Finishes warm and spicy. There’s a harmonious integration to this wine. This is a classic Barolo from a warm vintage that should age in interesting ways: it picks up some weight and structure on day 2 after opening. 94/100

Arnaldo Rivera Barolo Ravera 2022 Piemonte, Italy
14.5% alcohol. From five sites in this south-facing MGA. 30 months in cask. Just 4500 bottles made. Lovely aromatics with warm spices, some cedar hints, rose petal, iodine, wild strawberry and red cherry. The palate shows raspberry, cherry and strawberry with lovely texture and a hint of mint and pot pourri. This is a lovely wine with ripeness, detail, structure but also elegance. Some alcoholic warmth. 94/100

Arnaldo Rivera Barolo Bussia 2022 Piemonte, Italy
15% alcohol. From two sites facing southwest in this MGA. 30 months in cask, 3600 bottes. Lovely pale cherry red in colour. Some warmth on the nose, with red cherries and redcurrants as well as fine spicy notes. Elegant despite the alcohol, with dried herbs and some rose petal. The palate is textured, warm, elegant and has some smoothness from the high alcohol. There’s a real harmony and delicacy here, as well as ripe fruit and some alcoholic warmth. Lovely stuff and should age really well. 95/100

Arnaldo Rivera Verduno Pelaverga Suicristalli 2025 Piemonte, Italy
13.5% alcohol. Lighter red in colour. Wonderful aromatics of sweet cherry and aniseed with some leafy green notes and black pepper. The palate has lovely texture and detail, with a bit of structure and good acidity. Such a distinctive variety showing its best here. Massive drinkability, but also a bit of seriousness. I love it. 94/100

title: A tasting of 48 top artisan Champagnes from Berry Bros & Rudd
summary: This tasting brought together a brilliant selection of artisan Champagnes, all of which are being offered by UK wine merchant
content:
This tasting brought together a brilliant selection of artisan Champagnes, all of which are being offered by UK wine merchant Berry Bros & Rudd. These are a mix of grower Champagnes and also smaller houses that look like growers (often growers have had to supplement their own vineyard sources with bought-in grapes, but still behave like growers). Many of these were new to me.

The offer goes live on 6 October.

Champagne Clandestin Boreal Brut Nature 2023 France
This is Pinot Noir from the Côte des Bar. Taut and herb-laced with bice depth of apple and pear fruit. Overtly fruity but very fine. Expressive with delicate structure. 93/100

Champagne Clandestin Austral Brut Nature 2025 France
This is Pinot Noir from Buxières. Very fine with cherry and citrus fruit. Delicate and refined with a twist of grapefruit and some sour cherry on the finish. Pure and sleek. 93/100

Champagne Clandestin Trilogie KM1 2022 France
A series of three Brut Naturel Pinot Noirs from the same vineyard in Côte des Bar, but three different plots. Toast, minerals and some strong reduction, giving struck flint notes. Lovely savoury twist here with complex mineral, smoky, flinty detail. Remarkable. 96/100

Champagne Clandestin Trilogie KM2 2022 France
Nice mineral, smoky, flinty reductuin with fine cherries and spice. So expressive, layered and complex, but also really refined. 95/100

Champagne Clandestin Trilogie KM3 2022 France
Sour cherry, lime and pear with nice lemony detail. Refined with cherry and herb notes and such elegance. 95/100

Champagne Crété Chamberlin T.D.N -3.111 Grand Cru 2014 France
From Oger, stainless steel, no malolactic. 10.5 yeas on lees. Dosage 1 g/l. Lovely citrus, pear and white peach. Nice layered complexity with lime, sour cherry and a hint of baby sick. Lovely. 94/100

Champagne Crété Les Mazaux Permier Cru Vertis 2020 Chamberlin France
Dosage 1 g/l. This shows a creamy edge to the lively citrus fruit. Sour cherry and nice lemony detail with very subtle toastiness. Real finesse here. 93/100

Champagne Crété Chamberlin CDB Premier Cru 2019 France
Chardonnay from Cuis and Villenueve-Renneville, dosage 1 g/l. Taut with nice acid line. Linear with lemony detail and a hint of pithiness. Slight sour twist on the finish. Elegant and refined. 94/100

Champagne Fleury Blanc de Noirs NV France
From the Côte des Bar, this is Pinot Noir, dosage 3.4 g/l. Base year is 2021. Fresh, linea r and bright with herb-tinged, juicy fruit. Fresh and focused and very expressive. 92/100

Champagne Fleury Boléro 2006 France
Pinot Noir from the Côte des Bar, dosage 2.6 g/l. 50% in oak. This has a distinctive apple and fibreglass nose, as well as some notes of old casks. Powerful palate with vanilla, old wood and honey, with some sherry cask character. Distinctive and savoury. 91/100

Champagne Fleury Sonate Brut Nature 2014 France
85% Pinot Noir, 15% Chardonnay. Savoury, mineral, spicy and woody with nice weight. Quite savoury in style. 91/100

Champagne Franck Bonville Pur Avize Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs 2019 France
Chardonnay, dosage 3.3 g/l. Herbs, toast and lime on the nose. Ripe, generous toasty palate with bold fruit. Rounded and expressive. 92/100

Champagne Franck Bonville Pur Oger Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs 2019 France
Chardonnay, 3.3 g/l dosage. Citrus, pear and apple fruit with nice depth. Refined with some toasty notes. 93/100

Champagne Franck Bonville Pur Mesnil Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs 2019 France
Chardonnay, 2.5 g/l dosage. Nice weight here. Ripe, sleek pear, cherry and citrus fruit with good depth of fruit. 93/100

Champagne Franck Bonville Avize Grand Cru Extra Brut ‘Franck Bonville’ Millésime 2019 France
Chardonnay, dosage 3.3 g/l. Nice definition here with herbs, toast and citrus as well as ripe pear fruit. Good acidity with great balance. 93/100

Champagne Frederic Savart L’Ouverture Blanc de Noirs 1er Cru NV France
Pinot Noir, dosage 3.5 g/l. Nice weight here. Layered citrus and green apple fruit with some pear richness and a hint of toast. Lively citrus fruit dominates with a touch of cherry and slight saltiness on the finish. 93/100

Champagne Frederic Savart Bulle de Rosé 1er Cru Brut NV France
65% Pinot Noir, 30% Chardonnay, 5% Rouge d’Écueil. Dosage 4 g/l. Pale pink. Lovely bright cherry and toast with fine spicy hints. This is juicy, but there’s a mineral twist. 94/100

Champagne Lafalisse-Froissart Cuvée 045 Verzenay Grand Cru Extra Brut NV France
Base is 2023. 100% Pinot Noir, 16% reserve wines, small oak, dosage 4 g/l. Bright and linear with lovely refinement to the pure lemony fruit. Expressive and bright and quite mineral. 94/100

Champagne Lafalisse-Froissart Cuvée 276 Blanc de Boirs Verzenay Grand Cru Brut Nature NV France
100% Pinot Noir (base 2023, 10% reserve wines), small oak. Taut with complex aromatics. Precise, pure, lemony and focused with real precision. Very fine with stony minerality. 95/100

Champagne Lafalisse-Froissart Cuvée 791 Dizy Permier Cru Extra Brut NV France
From a plot called Les Terres Rouges, 100% Chardonnay (base 2023, 10% reserve wines), amphora and demi muids, dosage 3 g/l. Nice focus here with some depth to the crystalline citrus fruit. Such precision, and lovely intensity. 94/100

Champagne Madeleine Brochet 2020 France
From Taissy, 50% Pinot Noir, 50% Chardonnay, base wines in barrique with MLF, dosage 3 g/l. Rich and herby with toast and spice, and appealing apple notes. Broad and textured with real depth. Richer style. 94/100

Champagne Marguet Shaman Rosé 23 Grand Cru Zero Dosage NV France
Ambonnay/Bouzy. 76% Chardonnay, 24% Pinot Noir. Pale pink in colour. Nice pear and cherry with good depth and weight, finishing bright. Stylish and well defined. 93/100

Champagne Marguet Shaman 23 Grand Cru Zero Dosage NV France
Ambonnay. 92% Pinot Noir, 8% Chardonnay. Very open and expressive with sweet pear and cherry fruit. Nice texture, but a slight warning of impending mousiness on the palate? NR

Champagne Marguet Ambonnay Grand Cru Zero Dosage 2021 France
8% Pinot Noir, 92% Chardonnay. Lovely sour cherry and lemon and pear, with good acidity and lovely concentration. Nice sour twist on the palate. 94/100

Champagne Marguet Sapience Premier Cru Zero Dosage 2018 France
48% Pinot Meunier, 52% Pinot Noir. Layered, fruity and complex with mandarin, herbs and lime, as well as fresh cherries. Such elegance and focus here. 95/100

Champagne Marguet Les Crayères Grand Cru 2021 France
66% Chardonnay, 34% Pinot Noir. Complex and intense and layered with sour cherry and lime notes. Stony and mineral with nice tension and a savoury twist on the finish. 951/00

Champagne Marguet Le Parc Grand Cru Ambonnay 2021 France
100% Chardonnay. Taut with high acidity under the lime fruit. Vivid and alert with nice focus. Intense and mouthfilling. 94/100

Champagne Mathieu Godme2-Guillaume Terre de Verzy Grand Cru NV France
Base year 2020, 56% Pinot Noir, 44% Chardonnay, 3 g/l dosage. Sour cherries and lime. Nice intensity with crystalline citrus fruit, beautiful focus and some deopth. 94/100

Champagne Mathieu Godmé-Guillaume Terre de Verzenay Grand Cru NV France
Based on 2021, 100% Pinot Noir. 2 g/l dosage. Complex and layered with nice lime and lemon, as well as a sour acid line. Bright and vivid; fresh and complex. Real focus. 94/100

Champagne Mathieu Godmé-Guillaume VVV NV France
From Villers-Marmery, base is 2023, 33% reserves (2016, 2022), dosage 3 g/l. 100% Chardonnay. Lovely weight with lemons, pears and cherries. Textural with nice depth and elegance, but also a strong acid line. 94/100

Champagne Odysse 319 Avize Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs Brut NV France
Chardonnay, base year 2023, dosage 4.2 g/l. Fresh, textural and elegant, with lovely depth and weight. Harmonious with some generosity to the fruit, but it always stays elegant. So refined. 95/100

Champagne Odysse 319 Avize Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs 2021 France
Chardonnay, dosage 4.2 g/l. Complex with subtle toast and honey as well as ripe citrus and white peach fruit. Lovely depth and refinement to this textured wine. 95/100

Champagne Odysse 319 Jour 5 Chamery NV France
Base year 2022, equal parts Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier and Champagne. Dosage 4.2 g/l. Nice texture to this thrillingly balanced, nicely weighted Champagne, with pear, peach and cherry fruit as well as subtle toast. 95/100

Champagne Roger Coulon Heri Hodie NV France
Montagne de Reims, 100% Pinot Meunier, base 2022. Dosage 3 g/l. Aromatic nose of toast, herbs, cherries and mandarins. The palate shows appealing delicate cherry fruit with a touch of green apple. Lovely. 93/100

Champagne Roger Coulon Continuum NV France
Single plot Les Champs Chevalier, zero dosage. Amazing sour cherry and lime twist to the bold citrus fruit. Lovely acidity here. Expressive, mineral and taut. 94/100

Champagne Roger Coulon Blanc de Noirs 2015 France
Vrigny and Gueux. 50% Pinot Noir from Les Limons and 50% Pinot Meunier from Les Linguets, dosage 2.5 g/l. Complex, layered, rich and toasty with some herby notes. Cherry and lemon fruit with nice intensity. Powerful and weighty, finishing long. 95/100

Champagne Roger Coulon Les Hauts Partas 2019 France
Chouilly, Chardonnay. Zero dosage. Powerful and expressive with a nice savoury twist. Limey and intense, vivid and edgy. Real power. Focused and delicious. 95/100

Champagne Siret Reserve Perpetuelle NV France
From Côte des Bar and Côte des Blancs, 60% Pinot Noir, 40% Chardonnay. Dosage 3 g/l. This is complex, layered and precise with lemon and toast, as well as lovely depth. Intense, mineral and bold with some savoury complexity. 96/100

Champagne Siret Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs 2014 France
From Mesnil-sur-Oger and Oger, dosage 3 g/l. Such layered intensity here. Compact, salty and spicy with firm citrus fruit, some green apple and good acidity. Powerful and linear. 96/100

Champagne Siret Rosé de Saignée 2020 France
Pinot Noir, 3g/l dosage. Pale pink. Juicy with bright cherry and pear fruit as well a some strawberry. Lovely fruit, showing nice depth and refinement. 94/100

Champagne Siret Blanc de Noirs Côte des Bar Extra Brut 2018 France
Pinot Noir, dosage 3 g/l. Juicy, bright and powerful. Linear with nice fruitiness. Cherry and pear with good purity, and layers of flavour. So expressive. 95/100

Champagne Waris Hubert Sophos Blanc de Blancs Avize Grand Cru Extra Brut 2018 France
Dosage 3 g/l. Powerful and weighty with some toast, some woody savouriness, and good structure. Structured and intense in a gastronomic style. 94/100

Champagne Waris Hubert Blanche Blanc de Blancs Avize Grand Cru Extra Brut 2019 France
Dosage 3.3 g/l. Lively, multidimensional and precise, showing crystalline citrus fruit and some toasty depth. This has nice ripe peach fruit as well. So inviting. 94/100

Champagne Waris Hubert Albescent Blanc de Blancs Grand Cru NV France
Base wine 2022, dosage 3.8 g/l. Fruity, rich and expansive with ripe pear and peach fruit as well as some toast. Open and inviting, showing nice depth. 93/100

Champagne Waris Hubert Blanc de Blancs San Sulfites Ajoutés NV France
Base year 2023, dosage 3.4 g/l. Toast, honey and lemons. Open with some herby hints. Bright and expressive. 93/100

Champagne Aurore Casanova Puisieulx Chardonnay Les Peites Vignes NV France
Base 2022, 34% reserve wines. Dosage 3 g/l. Spicy with some woody hints as well as crystalline citrus fruit, with some herby detail. Very refined and complex, and quite gastronomic. 94/100

Champagne Aurore Casanova Puisieulx Pinot Noir Les Peites Vignes NV France
Base 2023 with 34% reserve wines. Fruity and vivid with bright citrus focus. Has cherry, pear and grapefruit with good definition and acidity. 94/100

Champagne Aurore Casanova Chardonnay Grand Cru NV France
Base 2023. Toast, vanilla, honey and lemons with some pear and a touch of rich peachy character. Very expressive. 93/100

title: Highlights: Waitrose No 1 Don Gaspar Dry Amontillado by Lustau
summary: I bought this Amontillado for a special recipe (to cook with) but it’s actually seriously good. I feel bad using
content:
I bought this Amontillado for a special recipe (to cook with) but it’s actually seriously good. I feel bad using it in cooking, when it’s a fine wine in its own right. Currently on offer at Waitrose. If I ever fell on hard times, I’d lean heavily on Sherry for my gastronomic drink hits. You can get really good examples at very reasonable prices still.

Waitrose No 1 Don Gaspar Dry Amontillado Sherry NV Spain
18% alcohol. This is made for Waitrose by Lustau, and it’s remarkably affordable for such a delicious wine. It has a beautifully complex nose with honey, tar, old wood, and some tangy citrus on the nose. It’s dry on the palate but with some richness, offering tangy, savoury, spicy notes alongside some crystalline citrus fruit. It offers amazing depth and complexity for the price. This is just beautiful and layered, with plenty of evolution and complexity. Warm, spicy and rich. 92/100 (£11.50 Waitrose, on offer from £14.50)

title: Restaurants: an amazing tasting menu at AngloThai, London
summary: Website: https://anglothai.co.uk/ A beautiful confluence of flavours, aesthetics and spot on service at AngloThai, complemented by a banging wine list.
content:
Website: https://anglothai.co.uk/

A beautiful confluence of flavours, aesthetics and spot on service at AngloThai, complemented by a banging wine list.

My first time at AngloThai this week. I’d met owners John and Desiree Chantarasak at an event at The Barbary a while back, so it was on my radar. John is half English/half Thai, hence the name, and this Michelin-starred restaurant opened its doors in November 2024 after many appearances as a pop-up, beginning in 2015.

The dining room is beautiful, and quite serene. Cleverly installed cork baffling in the ceiling looks decorative, but helps with keeping the noise down.

This is a tasting menu restaurant, and in the evenings it is £115 per head. This is not a cheap eat, but we loved it. The pace of the meal, the level of service, and the quality and imagination of the dishes is almost perfect.

The wine list needs a mention, because it has character and is really well thought out. There’s a strong emphasis on English wine, both fizzy and still. And there’s also strong Austrian representation. This is a gem of a list, although befitting to the fact that this is a Michelin-starred restaurant in a central London location, if feels slightly on the expensive side.

We drank a glass of the Langham Culver Classic, a beautiful English sparkling wine from one of the country’s top producers. I was tempted by a bottle from natural wine producer Woodfine, but in the end went for the Bonsai from Claus Preisinger in Austria’s Burgenland. This was a good choice: bright, refreshing, sappy and aromatic.

AngloThai is a destination restaurant. It would be wrong to think of it as a Thai restaurant, although there is a very strong influence with the flavours and the spicing. It’s unique. Everything is done brilliantly.
